newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * Tension has not subsided among protesting Jiu Valley miners who have rejected the government's offers.
Miners' leaders ruled out miners' invasion of the capital or roadblocks among possible new forms of protest.
* Miners from neighbouring areas on Wednesday joined the protest by Jiu Valley miners.
* Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea is expected to meet U.S. Vice President Albert Gore, to deliver a letter by Romanian President Emil Constantinescu in response to President Bill Clinton's letter.
* Romania will continue to lobby for admission to NATO and will not change its foreign policy priorities, Romania's Foreign Minister Adrian Severin told a news conference.

* A business forum in Paris has drawn more participants than expected, Romanian Senate chairman Petre Roman, on a visit to France, said. Industry Minister Calin Tariceanu and Bogdan Baltazar, deputy head of Romania's State Ownership Fund (FPS) presented Romania's investment and privatisation offer.
* Romanian-French political relations are excellent, but economic and cultural exchanges should be boosted, Roman said.
* Some 8,000 hectares of farmland were flooded in the northern Bihor and Salaj counties, but floods are expected to retreat over the next two days.
